Priya: Quick Q from product — in the town hall Elena said the competitive edge moves from model ownership to serving. Does that mean we should deprioritize new model integrations in favor of routing/caching/observability work?

Elena (CEO): Short answer: no, not deprioritize entirely. We want a balanced bet. Model quality matters, but the product win is predictable, cheap, and reliable inference. Put another way: models are the input; serving is how customers get consistent value at scale. We should tilt roadmap to optimize serving on top of the best models, not replace model work.

Ravi (CTO): To add — technically, features like smart routing, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles reduce customer cost per token by 2x-5x for many workloads. Those are higher-leverage for retention than adding one more model for a niche use-case.

Jake (Eng): Appreciate that. For Dedicated/Private customers, do we prioritize latency SLOs over cost optimization? A few enterprise accounts called asking about guaranteed p99 vs lower unit costs.

Maya (VP Product): Market segmentation: for mid-market SaaS we sell cost predictability and simple onboarding (so Optimize + hosted). For enterprise, it's SLAs, security, and private deployments. Roadmap should reflect both: baseline serving wins (caching/batching) then enterprise-grade fallbacks and region failover.

Elena (CEO): Competitor angle — many vendors pitch model breadth. Our message should be: "we make inference predictable and economical across deployments." Distinguish with concrete metrics (latency p99, $/M tokens, failover RTO). Avoid fuzzy promises — put numbers on the site/console.

Priya: Can we get a short battlecard with 3 competitor claims vs our counterpoints? Sales asked for one for next week.

Ravi (CTO): I'll draft a technical appendix showing kernel selection and where our runtime reduces tail latency. Include a simple table: scenario -> recommended config (e.g., short-chat -> dynamic batching + 8-bit quant, long-context -> KV cache + model variant).

Sam (Platform): Ops note — we can add a new per-route metric in Console showing "cost per 1k tokens" and a toggle to preview savings from caching. That helps customers see the economics live.

Jake (Eng): Follow-up: any change to prioritization of on-prem packaging? A couple prospects care about air-gapped installs.

Elena (CEO): Keep Private on the roadmap but focus initial engineering cycles on better observability + rollout controls for hosted/dedicated. Private gets a streamlined on-prem package (docs + install automation) after the core runtime wins land.

Priya: Thanks — can we capture these clarifications in a short follow-up doc and share with sales and solutions by EOD Friday? I can coordinate.

Elena (CEO): Yes. Action items: 1) @Ravi to produce tech appendix draft by Wed. 2) @Sam to mock Console metric by Thu. 3) @Priya to collate and publish the one-page positioning/battlecard by Fri. I'll review before it goes out. :thumbsup:
